references.text: Jesus taught daily in the temple: [ref:Luk 19:47|Luke 19:47] states that Jesus taught in the temple every day, which corresponds to his words here about being with them in the temple day after day without their seizing him.
[ref:Luk 21:37|Luke 21:37] describes Jesus' daily practice of teaching in the temple, which is the background for his remark that they did not lay hands on him then.
The parallel passage [ref:Matt 26:55|Matthew 26:55] records Jesus' similar words at his arrest: "Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me."
In [ref:Mark 14:49|Mark 14:49], Jesus says similarly that he was with them daily in the temple teaching, yet they did not seize him—a close parallel to this verse.
[ref:Joh 7:30|John 7:30] shows that no one laid hands on Jesus because his hour had not yet come, which explains why they did not seize him earlier in the temple.
Also [ref:Joh 8:20|John 8:20] emphasizes that no one seized Jesus because his hour had not yet come—God's sovereign timing over events.
[ref:Joh 12:27|John 12:27] speaks of the "hour" having arrived, in line with Jesus' words here that "this is your hour"—the decisive hour for suffering.
[ref:Ef 6:12|Ephesians 6:12] speaks of the struggle against the powers of darkness, which illuminates Jesus' reference to "the power of darkness" (ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ σκότους) in this verse.
[ref:Kol 1:13|Colossians 1:13] mentions "the power of darkness" (ἐξουσία τοῦ σκότους), the same expression Jesus uses here, and shows that God rescues us from this power.
[ref:Joh 3:19-20|John 3:19-20] contrasts light and darkness and says that those who do evil prefer darkness—illuminating Jesus' words that the arrest takes place at night under the power of darkness.
[ref:Jes 60:2|Isaiah 60:2] speaks of darkness covering the earth and peoples, a prophetic image that sheds light on Jesus' words about the power of darkness reigning in this decisive hour.
[ref:Luk 22:3|Luke 22:3] tells how Satan entered Judas, showing that the power of darkness was already at work and leading up to the arrest that Jesus mentions here.
